specification.family_title: Commit outcome after a connection or reply failure
specification.title: The connection is terminated after the last write, before COMMIT
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). The runner terminates that backend from its own connection, and waits until it has gone.
Wait settle_ms, so that the driver can observe the closed connection.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework attempts to commit.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When the connection or PostgreSQL's reply was lost around COMMIT, so that the client never received an acknowledgement of COMMIT, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: Positive control. Connection.setAutoCommit(false), then the work on that connection. Connection.commit() is reported as committed only when PgConnection.getTransactionState() was OPEN before the call. FAILED, which pgjdbc sets from ReadyForQuery status E, is reported as rolled_back after commit() returns; the command tag is not exposed. A thrown commit() is reported as failed and the connection is closed. A failed Connection.rollback(Savepoint) is followed by Connection.rollback(), not commit(). A thrown Connection.rollback() closes the connection and does not call setAutoCommit(true). Connection.setTransactionIsolation is called before setAutoCommit(false). One DriverManager connection is held. It is not a pool.

configuration.commit_outcome: Connection.commit(); rolled_back when PgConnection.getTransactionState() was FAILED

execution.form: Connection.setAutoCommit(false), the work, then Connection.commit() or Connection.rollback(). Writes use PreparedStatement.

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: After the last write, before the framework sends COMMIT.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and its transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: A connection error at COMMIT. No reply to COMMIT can arrive.

knowledge: Known not committed: the session ended before the framework tried to commit, so the driver refused to send COMMIT ("Client has encountered a connection error and is not queryable"). A report of rollback is justified; a report of success is not.

api_outcome.basis: Connection.commit() threw. The policy reports failed and closes the connection. It does not report a confirmed rollback.
api_outcome.contract: The correct jdbc-control policy uses Connection.setAutoCommit(false), Connection.commit, Connection.rollback, Connection.setSavepoint, Connection.rollback(Savepoint), and Connection.setTransactionIsolation. Java 21 Connection.commit() is void: "Makes all changes made since the previous commit/rollback permanent and releases any database locks currently held by this Connection object." It does not return a command tag. pgjdbc 42.7.14 PgConnection.commit sends COMMIT through executeTransactionCommand when getTransactionState() is not IDLE, and TransactionCommandHandler does not implement handleCommandStatus, so a COMMIT that PostgreSQL answers with the command tag ROLLBACK does not throw. Before commit(), the policy reads PgConnection.getTransactionState(), a public method. FAILED means the server has already sent ReadyForQuery status E (QueryExecutorImpl.receiveRFQ). If that state was FAILED and commit() returns, the policy reports rolled_back. It does not claim to have read the command tag. If commit() throws, the policy reports failed and closes the connection. If Connection.rollback() throws, the policy closes the connection and does not call setAutoCommit(true). Java 21 Connection.setAutoCommit says: "If this method is called during a transaction and the auto-commit mode is changed, the transaction is committed." pgjdbc 42.7.14 implements the change to true by calling commit() (PgConnection.setAutoCommit). A failed Connection.rollback(Savepoint) is followed by Connection.rollback() of the surrounding transaction, not by Connection.commit(). A requested isolation level is sent with Connection.setTransactionIsolation before setAutoCommit(false), while the driver state is IDLE.
